  Traffic Control Plan for the  Traffic Control Plan for the Fourth  of  Julv Parade -  Each year the City
  Fourth  of  July Parade  hosts community events to celebrate our nation' s independence. The largest
  event is the Fourth of July Parade on City streets through Old Town La Verne.
  The City Engineer prepared a traffic control plan for the parade route. Formal
  adoption of this plan by the City Council will limit the City' s liability exposure by
  providing design immunity.

  Public Works Director Igoe recommended that the City Council adopt the traffic
  control  plan  for the Fourth  of  July Parade. Approved as recommended by
  staff:

  Reappointment  Matthew  Forgey and Zuhey Espinoza expired on June 30, 2022. While Dr.

  decided to no longer continue as a Board Member.

  Board seat will be advertised and after a recommendation from the Board,
  will be presented to the Mayor and City Council at a future meeting for
  appointment.  Approved as recommended.

5.  Presentations/  Pride  Month  Mayor Hepburn, on behalf of the City Council, presented a Proclamation
  proclaiming the Month of June 2022 as" Pride Month" in support of the
  Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer( LGBTQ) community as they
  declare their pride in who they are and whom they love and reaffirming the
  City' s shared values of cultural awareness, social inclusion, compassion,
  equity, and diversity. Ryan Harrison; Susan Boyer; Zandra Wagoner; and Julia
  Wheeler accepted the proclamation and thanked the City Council.

  rendered the Fire Department' s current contract with our Nurse Educator
  invalid and the department is now in violation  of  Department  of  Labor laws.  To

  rectify this,  staff recommends approval of an agreement with UCLA to
  conduct continuing education in prehospital and emergency medicine for

  patient  care.

  agreement with  the UCLA  Pre- hospital EMS Educator  Program.  This

  partnership will greatly enhance the delivery of our EMS Continuing
  Education and Quality Improvement programs to better meet the needs of
  our department, County EMS standards, and the citizens that we serve.
  Approved.

11.  Temporary Employment  Assistant to the City Manager Ranells reported on the temporary employment
  Agreement  for Interim  Fire  agreement for  Interim  Fire Battalion Chief. He stated that Fire Battalion Chief
  Battalion Chief  Kevin Greenway has retired from the City of La Verne effective June 15, 2022,
  after being employed by the City for 20 years. In order to minimize disruption
  to the Fire Department resulting from this loss of institutional and operational
  knowledge, the City is interested in retaining his services until the end of the
  fiscal year.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was  none.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, June 20, 2022, Page 8.

  It was moved by Crosby, seconded by Davis, and unanimously carried
  authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement with Kevin Greenway to
  provide temporary, part- time employment.
